title: Quantum-Relativistic Anomalous Proper Time
abstract: We investigate surprising consequences of the hypothesis that gravity and proper time obey the quantum superposition principle. We show that, for a massive body prepared in a superposition of two positions and post-selected in a suitable final state, the elapsed proper time in another region of space can assume an anomalous effective value lying outside the range allowed by classical general relativity. Remarkably, the effective elapsed proper time can even become negative, corresponding to an effective evolution backward in time. We also propose an experiment to observe an anomalous effective proper time associated with the internal degrees of freedom of a quantum particle in an interferometer under Earth's gravitational field. The proposed experiment is, in principle, feasible with current technology, and its realization could provide the first experimental evidence of an interplay between quantum mechanics and general relativity beyond the effects of the Newtonian potential in flat spacetime.
summary: This paper explores what happens if proper time itself is subject to quantum superposition. By analyzing an interferometer setup, the authors predict that the measured effective proper time can take anomalous values, even becoming negative. This offers a novel, potentially observable test for quantum gravity effects using high-precision atomic interferometry.
main_problem: The paper investigates the consequences of assuming that gravity and proper time obey the quantum superposition principle, leading to potentially anomalous time evolution.
main_result: The effective elapsed proper time ($\tau_{ef}$) can assume values outside the classically allowed range, potentially becoming negative, suggesting a non-classical interaction between quantum mechanics and general relativity.
method: The analysis uses quantum mechanical formalism (Schrödinger equation) applied to a source particle in a superposition state to calculate the effective proper time experienced by a nearby probe system.
model_or_system: The primary model involves a source particle in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer setup interacting with a probe system whose proper time evolution is measured in Earth's gravitational field. The Hamiltonian is treated in the weak field limit.
key_observables: The effective elapsed proper time ($\tau_{ef}$), and the resulting interference phase shift ($\theta_{ef}$).
important_parameters: The relative difference in proper times ($\tau_B - \tau_A$) and the precision achievable by atomic clocks ($\sim 10^{-19}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the weak field approximation and assumes that decoherence can be managed to observe the predicted quantum interference effects.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the interferometer scheme for observing $\tau_{ef}$. Figure 2 shows $\tau_{ef}$ deviating from classical bounds based on superposition coefficients. Figure 3 proposes an alternative scheme using atomic clocks in Earth's field.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by analyzing the effective proper time ($\tau_{ef}$) derived from the superposition of paths, comparing different experimental schemes (source superposition vs. clock superposition), and concluding with the feasibility and implications of observing this anomalous time evolution.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum mechanics and general relativity by proposing an observable signature—an anomalous proper time—that would confirm quantum gravitational effects beyond standard Newtonian approximations.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Scheme to obtain an anomalous proper time for the probe quantum system. A source massive quantum particle has two possible paths in a 1D Mach-Zehnder interferome- ter. If the source mass propagates along path A, closer to the origin, a clock in the probe system runs slower than if the source mass propagates along path B, farther away. The clock pointer then becomes entangled with the position of the source mass in the superposition state depicted in the figure. A post-selection of the source mass at the exit of the interfer- ometer can generate an effective elapsed proper time for the probe system outside what is permitted by general relativity.

FIG. 3. Proposed scheme to verify an anomalous proper time. A quantum particle with a internal degree of freedom work- ing as a clock propagates in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer under Earth’s gravitational field g. BS1 and BS2 are beam splitters. Since the proper time for the particle internal de- gree of freedom runs faster for a higher gravitational poten- tial, the clock pointer will be entangled with the particle path, in the superposition state depicted in the figure. Depending on the particular exit the particle leaves the interferometer, the elapsed proper time for the clock may be outside what is permitted by general relativity, what could be experimentally verified.
